newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Ragged Australian bonds stabilise in SYCOM.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Ragged Australian bonds stabilise in SYCOM.

text.p: Australian bond futures stabilised during the SYCOM session, albeit in a relatively thin turnover, after Monday's dayside trade saw a further corrective sell-off from last week's two month highs.
The June 10-year bond futures contract ended the afterhours session at 92.035 compared with Monday's 92.010 pit close and after touching a low of 91.990.

The contract made a decisive breakdown through the 92.080/92.010 support area are early on Monday, which is now likely to turn into resistance on any upside moves, and the sell-off gathered pace once computerised hedge funds stepped in.
The market is now finding some support just below the psychological 92.000 level, but a firmer barrier is seen at 91.950 before the market tests 91.850, analysts said.

A firmer tone in U.S. Treasuries on Monday helped the local market stabilise. However, a cautionary stance is likely to prevail ahead of the first of this week's key U.S. indicators later on Tuesday with the release of the first quarter employment index.
Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan is also due to address the International Monetary Fund/World Bank spring meeting in Washinton.

There is no local economic data out of Australia until Wednesday's release of the March balance of goods and services, although more trading emphasis will be on the outcome of Thursday's first quarter average weekly ordinary time earnings.
Victorian Treasurer Alan Stockdale will hand down the 1997/98 budget to the state parliament at 3.00 p.m. (0500 GMT).
